title: Court-Safe Esper Machine From Bystander Video
one_liner: Blade Runner's Esper machine, made honest: a scaled, non-generative 3D reconstruction of an accident scene from mixed dashcam, doorbell, CCTV and phone clips, with error bars built to survive an admissibility challenge.
customer: Personal-injury law firms, insurer subrogation and special-investigation units, defense counsel and municipal risk managers, initially in disputed-liability vehicle and pedestrian cases with three or more video clips.
problem: Cases turn on several shaky clips. Traditional reconstruction by an expert costs thousands of dollars and takes weeks. Generative 'enhancement' gets challenged or excluded because AI invents pixels, and Gaussian-splat models look convincing but have no verified real-world scale.
solution: Ingest all clips, time-sync them (audio fingerprints, sirens, shared events), solve camera poses, and recover metric scale automatically from regulated-size objects in frame: lane-stripe cycles, stop and speed signs, crosswalk widths, license plates and standard curb heights. Output a measurable model with per-measurement error bars and a 'no generated pixels' guarantee (every pixel traceable to a source frame), plus vehicle speed and trajectory estimates and sightline views ('could the driver see the pedestrian?'). A partner licensed reconstructionist signs the report and serves as expert of record.
why_now: Feed-forward multi-view reconstruction and Gaussian splatting made casual-video reconstruction cheap in the last two years. Courts and defense bars are actively litigating AI-enhanced video. Doorbell, dashcam and storefront cameras mean most incidents now have several angles.
revenue_model: $900-2,500 per case, a discount tier for firms on subscription, and an expert-testimony fee split with the reconstructionist.
non_obvious_insight: Admissibility, not photorealism, is the product. Lawyers would rather have an ugly model with error bars than a beautiful hallucination, and automatic metric scale from objects whose dimensions are set by traffic-control standards is the unlock that separates this from generic splat tools and from drone-only videogrammetry.
first_30_days: Recruit one reconstructionist as expert of record. Offer 10 PI firms a free second-opinion reconstruction on live cases with at least three clips, then charge $1,200 for the next. Target five paying cases by day 90 and a written methods statement reviewed by a litigator.

title: Buy Oil-Heat Dealers, Sell Heat Pumps
one_liner: Acquire retiring Northeast heating-oil dealers for their loyal customers and boiler-failure moments, run the fuel business as a cash annuity, and convert customers to heat pumps.
customer: Northeast homeowners heating with oil (from about 19% of homes in New York to 59% in Maine), income-qualified households with state and utility rebates, and dealer owners who want a succession exit.
problem: Oil-only dealers face policy-driven volume decline and aging owners with no successors, yet each holds 1,000 to 5,000 loyal customers with known equipment ages. Heat pump installers pay high customer-acquisition costs and lack trust. The federal 25C credit ended for systems placed in service after 2025, so state programs and CAC decide winners.
solution: Acquire small dealers, keep the local brand, drivers and techs. AI ops: a propensity model using tank size, burner age, delivery volume and home age to time an offer when a boiler is about to fail, virtual site surveys and load calcs from photos, automated rebate and financing paperwork, retraining of drivers and technicians for heat pump service, and route optimization to protect fuel cash flow during the transition. Sell 'heat-as-a-service' subscriptions with dual-fuel backup.
why_now: Post-2025, incentives shifted to state and utility programs (Massachusetts, New York, Maine and others), and HEEHRA rebates of up to $8,000 for income-qualified households continue where states have launched. Heat pump technology is mature for cold climates. Dealer owners are aging, and the customer relationship is the hard-to-buy asset.
revenue_model: Fuel margin as the cash cow, service contracts, heat pump installs at roughly $15k to $25k per job, and financing spreads. Acquisition financed with seller notes and SBA 7(a).
non_obvious_insight: Electrification's scarce asset is trust plus the moment a boiler dies. Oil dealers already own both, and they are the only local business that knows each home's system age and gets the 2 a.m. January call. Buy the relationship and use the declining fuel business to fund the conversion.
first_30_days: List 50 independent dealers within a two-hour radius from state oilheat associations. Approach five owners over 60 with seller-financed offers. Before buying, start as a white-label heat pump conversion partner that rev-shares with dealers on their customers, which can produce first revenue in 60 to 90 days.

title: Swarf Stabilization for New US Magnet Plants
one_liner: Hazmat-grade stabilization, transport and recycler routing for the pyrophoric NdFeB grinding swarf that new US magnet plants will produce in tonnes.
customer: New and expanding US sintered-magnet makers and independent magnet grinding shops, who pay per-kg handling. Recyclers and re-melters are the downstream buyers.
problem: US magnet capacity is ramping (MP Materials broke ground on a Texas magnet campus in Feb 2026 on a DoD-backed deal). Machining and grinding turn a large share of sintered NdFeB, often 20-30%, into oil-wet, self-heating swarf and sludge. It is hard to classify, ship and store, so it drifts to overseas buyers or hazardous-waste disposal.
solution: An inerting and oil-immersion protocol, DOT-compliant packaging for self-heating solids, permitted storage through a partner, and routing to domestic recyclers or re-melters. It comes with a mass-balance certificate that lets the magnet maker claim recycled content to defense and EU customers.
why_now: Trace the chain: DoD equity and DPA-style support create new US magnet plants, which create swarf, which becomes a fire and compliance problem with no dedicated service. EU rare-earth recycled-content obligations phase in 2028-2032, and recyclers such as Cyclic Materials are funded and hunting for clean feed.
revenue_model: Handling fee per kg, plus a revenue share of recovered oxide or alloy value from recyclers, plus an annual compliance retainer.
non_obvious_insight: The near-term rare-earth urban mine is inside the factory. Swarf is clean, known-composition and available in tonnes before any end-of-life magnet wave arrives.
first_30_days: Call EHS heads at the 5 new or ramping magnet plants and 10 grinding shops. Offer a free swarf audit to quantify tonnage and value. Line up a hazmat-permitted storage and transport partner and one recycler offtake. Run a first pilot shipment.

title: Pharmacy Friendly Calls, Paid by Adherence Stars
one_liner: Independent pharmacies run weekly human-led friendship calls to isolated refill customers, funded by the Medicare adherence performance that loneliness quietly erodes.
customer: Independent community pharmacies (roughly 18,000 in the US) paying $500-1,200 a month per store, later reimbursed through Medicare Advantage and Part D plan performance and MTM contracts.
problem: Isolated older adults skip refills. Adherence measures for diabetes, RAS-antagonist and statin drugs carry triple weight in Medicare Star ratings, so plans pay for every point. Older adults distrust AI companions (Pew, Jun 2026: 40-46% of 65+ are 'unsure' whether chatbots help or hurt), and startup elder-companion services lack a trusted local face. The corner pharmacist has that trust and a list of exactly who is isolated.
solution: A 'Pharmacy Pal' program. Each store enrolls 40-80 living-alone or homebound refill customers. A paid part-time caller (a retiree or pharmacy tech) makes a weekly 10-minute call using an AI-prepared brief (last call notes, refill gaps, birthdays), and also does a twice-monthly delivery run. Software covers rosters, call briefs, refill-gap alerts and a proportion-of-days-covered dashboard the pharmacy can show plans. The AI never talks to the patient.
why_now: Chain-store closures (Rite Aid's 2025 wind-down among them) made independents the last local pharmacy for many seniors. Plans are squeezed on Star bonuses and margins and want cheap, measurable adherence levers. Pew's 2026 data show older adults distrust chatbots, which reopens the case for human-led programs.
revenue_model: $12-18 per enrolled patient per month, paid by the pharmacy out of retained refills, delivery fees and plan MTM or performance-network payments. Phase two is direct plan contracts priced on measured adherence lift.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders look for an elder-companion buyer among families and social-service agencies. The real loneliness budget for older adults sits inside Star-rating adherence economics, and the trusted delivery channel is the local pharmacist, not an app.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 independent pharmacies through state pharmacist associations and PSAO newsletters. Each pulls 40 patients from refill-gap reports. Run the calls manually with a spreadsheet and an LLM-generated brief. Measure adherence lift against matched non-enrolled patients over 90 days. Charge $500 a month per store from the start.

title: Independent Collateral Audits for GPU-Backed Loans
one_liner: A floorplan-audit business for private credit: physically verify, monitor and value the GPUs that secure a fast-growing pile of debt.
customer: Mid-market private credit funds, family-office lenders, equipment-finance arms and ABS trustees with GPU-backed facilities. Neocloud borrowers are a second payer, since verified collateral lowers their cost of capital.
problem: Over $20 billion of GPU-backed debt existed by early 2026, typically advancing 50-70% of appraised value, yet the resale value depends on obsolescence assumptions that are unsettled. Two large neoclouds use depreciation schedules of six and four years on similar hardware. Lenders mostly rely on borrower-provided reports and cannot see the rack, so they cannot confirm that serial numbers exist, are powered, are utilized and are located where the collateral schedule says.
solution: Borrow the car-dealer floorplan audit playbook. Field technicians verify serial numbers via BMC/IPMI readouts and photos, check rack location and power draw, sample cluster utilization through read-only telemetry attestations, review hosting contracts, insurance and cooling health, and grade condition. Deliver a quarterly report to the lender, then build continuous monitoring and a published GPU residual-value index.
why_now: GPU-backed credit scaled from experiment to institutional product in 2025-26. The next-generation architecture transition in 2026 and the rolling-off of 2023-24 contracts make collateral quality the central credit question, and lenders new to the asset class have no in-house inspectors.
revenue_model: $5-25k per site audit and $2-8k per month for monitoring, paid by lenders and sometimes borrowers. Later, data license revenue from the residual-value index.
non_obvious_insight: A GPU loan looks like equipment finance but behaves like tech inventory concentrated in a few sites. The missing service is not analytics but a trusted human in the room. Aircraft and auto-floorplan lenders solved this decades ago, and a small team of ex-data-center technicians plus one equipment-finance lawyer can do the same.
first_30_days: Team up two ex-data-center technicians with an equipment-finance lawyer. Approach 10 mid-market lenders and GPU-lease brokers. Offer one first audit at cost for a lender-borrower pair. Standardize the deliverable (serial check, photos, power and uptime, contract review) and publish an anonymized sample report to win the next five audits.

title: Work-Authorization Continuity Benefit for Care Employers
one_liner: An employer-paid benefit that screens every care worker for legal pathways, tracks EAD renewals and reverification, and plans backfill.
customer: Home-care agencies, nursing homes and assisted-living groups with 50-2,000 workers, especially in NY, FL, MA, MN, WI and CA, and staffing agencies.
problem: 30% of direct care workers are immigrants (60% in New York), and about 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4. At least one in five immigrant direct-care workers come from countries hit by the 75-country visa pause. With turnover already at 77-80%, losing staff means closed beds, and few workers have been screened for family, asylum, adjustment or other pathways.
solution: A per-worker monthly benefit: confidential attorney-led status screening and pathway triage, EAD and renewal tracking with on-time filing, an I-9 reverification calendar with non-discriminatory templates, workforce-at-risk forecasting by site and date, and fast backfill through a partner training school. Employers see aggregate risk, not individual status.
why_now: The 2026 visa pause, TPS terminations and a DOL proposal to roll back home-care wage protections hit at once, and Wisconsin agencies say they're 'just not able to take new clients.' Employers need something other than lobbying.
revenue_model: $8-15 per worker per month (employer-paid), plus filing fees with 20-30% margin and optional filing-fee financing.
non_obvious_insight: Immigration compliance is treated as static HR paperwork, but for care employers it is now a retention and continuity problem. Attorney-led screening can surface pathways that keep workers, which is worth thousands per retained caregiver.
first_30_days: Partner with an immigration law firm and a Haitian community organization, sign three agencies with Haitian-heavy workforces (NY, FL, MA), and pilot with 200 workers.

title: Cube Receipt: Win LTL Reclass and Reweigh Disputes
one_liner: A 45-second phone-based dimension-and-weight capture at the shipper's dock produces a timestamped, tamper-evident record attached to the BOL, then used to contest LTL carrier reclass and reweigh charges on contingency.
customer: Small and mid-size B2B shippers with $50K-$2M in annual LTL spend (furniture and home-goods makers, craft food and beverage, DTC brands shipping pallets, HVAC and parts distributors), plus small brokers who arrange LTL and absorb the adjustments when customers refuse to pay.
problem: The NMFC update on July 19, 2025 moved a large number of item numbers to density-based classification. Carriers reweigh and re-dimension freight at terminals with automated dimensioners and bill the corrected class, commonly a $30-$75 fee plus a 20-50% rate uplift. The shipper has no evidence of what actually left the dock, so the carrier's inspection is judge and jury. Most shippers just pay, and brokers who booked the load eat a share when the customer will not.
solution: A mobile app (iPhone LiDAR or camera) walks the packer through a pallet capture: dimensions with a reference marker, weight from a scale photo or entry, density and class check, wrap-bulge and overhang warnings, then hash and timestamp. It generates a QR sticker and a PDF appended to the BOL. When an adjustment invoice arrives (ingested from carrier emails or the freight audit feed), it auto-files the dispute with the evidence, tracks the carrier response, and takes a share of money recovered. It also flags pre-shipment problems, such as stretch-wrap bulge and pallet lip that inflate carrier-measured cube.
why_now: The July 2025 NMFC density shift is still generating adjustment invoices in 2026, and shippers are still learning the new classes. Phone LiDAR is ubiquitous, and carrier dimensioners are now the default at terminals, which makes source-side evidence the missing counterweight.
revenue_model: 25-30% of recovered adjustment charges (contingency), or $99-$299/month per dock. White-label to brokers at about $0.75 per shipment.
non_obvious_insight: Reclass is an evidence-asymmetry game, not a classification problem. The carrier's dimensioner records at the terminal and the shipper has nothing from the source. Terminal cube often includes bulging wrap and the pallet lip. A record made at tender time beats an after-the-fact photo inside the dispute window. Brokers see this daily in adjustment invoices but treat it as a cost of doing business rather than a product.
first_30_days: Approach 10 brokers who place LTL for small shippers. Each has adjustment invoices sitting in AR. Take six months of them, run manual disputes on contingency using whatever photos the shippers have, and log win rates by carrier. Build a no-code capture form (photo checklist plus timestamp) and put it on 3 shippers' docks. Use the win-rate data to sell the app.

title: Polling-Agent Payroll With Proof-of-Presence Release
one_liner: Pay each party or observer polling-unit agent directly, releasing money only after a geo-fenced arrival selfie and a result-sheet photo, so nothing gets skimmed on the way down.
customer: Election observer NGOs and civic groups (donor-funded, need audit trails) first. Then campaign directorates of governorship, National Assembly and state assembly candidates across parties. Later, any organisation paying temporary field staff.
problem: Election day is Nigeria's biggest one-day distribution of small payments. Agent allowances travel as lump sums from state to LGA to ward to polling-unit coordinators. Each layer keeps a cut, so a N20k allocation often reaches the agent as N5k. Agents then no-show, or get bought by the other side. Campaign directors know this leakage exists but have no proof and no tool. Since the 2023 cash scarcity, everything has been done by ad-hoc bank transfers and screenshots.
solution: A WhatsApp, USSD and light-Android flow. The party or NGO uploads its INEC-submitted agent list. Each agent gets a wallet or bank payout. Payment is released in tranches: 50% on a geo-fenced 7:30am arrival check-in, 50% on upload of the EC8A result-sheet photo. A coordinator dashboard shows attendance heat-maps and unpaid or unresponsive units in real time. Payments are for presence and documentation only, never for outcomes. Amounts are capped and pre-approved, and a spend report is produced for Electoral Act limits. The platform is strictly non-partisan and serves any party on identical terms.
why_now: INEC has fixed the presidential and National Assembly elections for 16 January 2027 and the governorship and state assembly polls for 6 February 2027. Parties must submit polling-agent names by 10 December 2026 and 6 January 2027. The campaign season is open now, with the Electoral Act 2026 in force. Nigeria has roughly 177,000 polling units, and every serious party wants an agent in each. LLM-based photo checks and cheap bulk-payout APIs (Paystack, Flutterwave, Monnify transfers) make a small team viable. The deadline forces a fast pilot.
revenue_model: 2-3% fee on disbursed allowances, plus a per-agent onboarding fee of about N300-500. Campaigns and NGOs pay a flat SaaS fee for the dashboard and audit pack. Float on pre-funded wallets adds a small yield. After the elections, the same engine is resold as conditional-release payroll for temporary field workers: brand activations, survey and census enumerators, NGO vaccination and outreach drives.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer does not want digital payments. The buyer wants proof that the last person in a 5-layer cash chain actually showed up and got paid. Coordinators lose money to leakage, and that gives campaign principals a reason to bypass the middle layers. The wedge is fraud reduction, not fintech. A conditional-release payment is also more valuable as a workforce-verification product than as a payment product.
first_30_days: Build the check-in and photo flow on top of an existing payout API. Offer it free to one observer NGO or a single state-assembly campaign for a live Ekiti, Osun or by-election dry run, plus a paid pilot for a governorship candidate. Recruit 5 ward coordinators and get 500 agents paid in the first test. Approach NGO election-observation networks and donor programme officers, who already need audit trails. Get written non-partisan and INEC-compliance opinions from a lawyer before the first party contract. Price the first campaign at cost to get case studies.

title: Recycled-Content Claim Defense Files
one_liner: Litigation-grade, SKU-level substantiation files for recycled-content claims, built on purchase-to-claim reconciliation rather than more certificates.
customer: General counsel and heads of sustainability at mid-market consumer brands ($100M-$2B revenue) with 'recycled' claims on pack, and retailer private-label teams.
problem: California vetoed AB 2253 (recycled-content claim substantiation) citing 'economic headwinds.' State PCR mandates are slipping (NJ to 2029). Mass-balance accounting is contested and no standard exists. Brands keep making claims for retailers and consumers, while the burden of proving them lands on legal departments via plaintiffs, AGs and retailer audits.
solution: A SKU-level claim file: verify supplier certificates, reconcile volume of certified resin bought against recycled-content claims across all SKUs, and produce a plain-language legal memo on which claims are safe. Add an annual refresh with change alerts. Partner with an insurer for defense-cost coverage credits.
why_now: The veto removed the one route to a state safe harbor and the mandate delays weaken the compliance pretext, so brands are exposed to claim risk without clear rules. Two years of contested mass-balance debate leave no accepted method.
revenue_model: $3-8K per SKU family for the initial file, $20-60K per year retainer, and referral fees from insurers and law firms.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody is short of certificates. Brands are short of reconciliation: a certificate proves a supplier's volume, not that a brand's claims across 400 SKUs are arithmetically supportable.
first_30_days: Build a spreadsheet reconciliation template. Partner with one litigation-defense law firm. Scrape retail listings for '% recycled' claims to find targets. Sell 5 paid claim audits at about $5K each.

title: Savings Groups Finance Apprenticeships via Income-Share
angle: Education, credentialing and skills after AI x Emerging markets leapfrogging
one_liner: A mobile-money tool that lets a village savings group use its year-end share-out to pay a workshop for a young member's apprenticeship and starter toolkit, then collect 10-12% of that apprentice's income for two years back into the group.
customer: Village savings and loan groups, chamas and small SACCOs of 20-30 members in Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania, which pay the fees. Workshops and TVET trainers who get paid upfront, and employers such as solar installers who want certified graduates, pay referral and placement fees.
problem: Formal training plus tools costs $150-500, which is out of reach for a household living on irregular farm income. Youth have no credit history. Income-share agreements have mostly failed in rich countries because income verification and collection cost more than the loan. Meanwhile savings groups hold a pile of cash at each year-end share-out and have few productive places to put it.
solution: A USSD and WhatsApp workflow. The group votes on a candidate. The group pays the trainer in tranches confirmed by attendance and milestone photos. The tool collects a set share of the graduate's mobile-money income into the group ledger, and members receive returns pro rata. Social collateral does the enforcement, so no bureau or aggregator is needed. Legally it is structured as an income-linked group loan, not a security.
why_now: Sandi AI reports 10,000+ farmer groups across Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania pooling savings for solar irrigation instead of borrowing, so groups will invest pooled money in productive assets. Africa's solar and battery installs are growing about 45% a year and 75% of that is distributed, which creates paid technician work. With six seed rounds for every Series A, outside capital is scarce and group capital is the reachable pool. Reported pressure on Gulf remittances, about $50bn at risk, weakens family-funded schooling.
revenue_model: A 4% origination fee on training payments, 1% of repayments, and 5-8% referral fees from trainers and tool vendors. Placement fees of about $20 per graduate come from installers and employers. Youth-employment funders can pay $100-200 per verified income outcome, which is what makes the thin margin work at small scale.
non_obvious_insight: The income-share agreement broke in rich countries on enforcement, and a savings group solves enforcement at zero marginal cost because members know the apprentice, the workshop and the family. The year-end share-out also lands in December, right before January apprenticeship intake, so a timing mismatch becomes a built-in cash cycle.
first_30_days: Partner with a savings-group promoter NGO or a platform like Sandi AI. Choose five groups within three months of their share-out. Sign three workshops (welding, solar installation, motorcycle repair or tailoring) to milestone-based payment. Launch 10 apprenticeships worth $3-4k, funded by the groups' own money plus a small first-loss guarantee from a grant. Track progress by photo and voice notes on WhatsApp, and record the first income repayments.

title: Dock Tax: Pricing Every Shipper Facility's Hidden Premium
one_liner: Use pooled broker quote and cover data to compute the exact per-load premium carriers add to any lane touching each bad dock, then sell shippers a ranked 'fix these five docks' report with dollar savings attached.
customer: VPs of supply chain and transportation procurement at mid-market shippers with $5M-$80M in truckload spend across 8-100 facilities (food and beverage, building products, paper and packaging, PE-backed manufacturers). Secondary: PE operating partners. A second product goes to brokers as a pre-quote facility difficulty score.
problem: Shippers think their rates reflect lane and market. Brokers know the rate also carries a facility premium for long dwell, no appointments, lumper games, no restrooms or parking, and dock staff who vanish at lunch. Our quotes to those docks quietly run $50-$300 a load higher, or the load is skipped by carriers and covered at the last minute at a spot premium. The shipper never sees it because it is buried in the broker's margin, and the broker profits from it, so the broker will never tell them.
solution: Pool anonymized quote-request, time-to-cover, rate-versus-benchmark and carrier-decline-reason data from 10-30 participating small brokers, who get a free facility difficulty score for pre-quoting in return. Run a regression of rate against market benchmark with facility fixed effects. Add dwell data from ELD partners or driver surveys. Deliver a Dock Tax Report: per-facility annualized premium in dollars, ranked, with a fix playbook (appointment windows, extended hours, drop-trailer conversion, driver amenities, lumper policy) and a re-bid plan on the affected lanes.
why_now: Driver supply has tightened through 2025-26 enforcement (English-proficiency out-of-service enforcement, non-domiciled CDL restrictions, authority revocations), which makes carriers pickier about which docks they will visit. AI arrival prediction and automated detention data from TMS integrations are making dwell data cheap. Vendor sources report that moving from first-come-first-served to scheduled appointments cuts dwell 30-50% within about 90 days, so the fix is proven and the ROI is easy to state.
revenue_model: $15K-$40K per shipper report or quarterly engagement, or 15-20% of first-year verified savings. Broker-side subscription of $200-$500/month for pre-quote facility scores builds the data flywheel.
non_obvious_insight: The dock tax is the only freight cost that is invisible to the payer and visible to everyone else. Every broker keeps a mental list of facilities where they never quote under a floor, and colleagues have nicknames for them, but nobody has priced that list for the shipper. Shippers will trust a neutral third party far more than their own broker, because the broker earns from the premium.
first_30_days: Get 8 brokers to share 90 days of anonymized quote and cover data for 20 named facilities in a shared sheet. Build the first regression by hand in a notebook. Cold-message 30 transportation directors on LinkedIn with a free 'your three worst docks' teaser built from the pooled data and public driver reviews, and sell 3 pilots at $7.5K. Give contributing brokers a per-facility difficulty lookup so they keep feeding the pool.

title: Blue UAS Bill-of-Materials Origin Auditor
one_liner: Part-by-part origin verification so 60,000-drone orders do not fail on hidden Chinese-origin motors, radios and cameras.
customer: Drone makers and their integrators selling to DoD and public safety, and the primes that must certify their subcontractors' parts.
problem: Compliance requires proving that components meet domestic-content and ownership rules, but sub-tier motors, ESCs, batteries and cameras often trace to opaque distributors. Manufacturers self-certify with spreadsheets and hope a re-labelled part is not found mid-contract.
solution: Upload a BOM and receive origin confidence per part. Cross-check import records, distributor invoices, factory databases and optional lab teardown or spectrum fingerprinting of sample units. Deliver an auditor-ready dossier and alerts when a supplier changes source.
why_now: Drone Dominance orders make component provenance a gating item for tens of thousands of units. About 48 defense firms are IPO candidates and want clean compliance records. Gauntlet winners must scale quickly and can't afford a failed audit (verify statutory citations).
revenue_model: $5-25K per BOM audit, $2-8K per month for monitoring, and per-sample teardown fees.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not certification but suppliers' unofficial data. Trade-data analytics plus teardown labs beat legal-only compliance firms because they can catch a repackaged part.
first_30_days: Audit 3 drone BOMs for free to build a dataset. Hire a customs-data analyst and a contract RF engineer. Pitch Gauntlet participants directly.

title: Circle Cue: Name Whispers for Early Dementia
one_liner: Consent-only Bluetooth badges let earbuds whisper who a person is and one line of context to someone with mild cognitive impairment, with no cameras and no face recognition.
customer: Families of people with mild cognitive impairment or early Alzheimer's ($149 kit plus $15 a month), memory cafes, senior centers and faith groups, and later Medicare Advantage plans and dementia-care programs.
problem: People in early dementia often withdraw because forgetting names is humiliating, and caregivers watch the social world shrink. Face-recognition glasses are legally and ethically fraught (biometric-privacy laws), and dementia technology focuses on safety tracking rather than social participation.
solution: Circle members (family, neighbors, club regulars) opt in by wearing small Bluetooth badges with rotating IDs. The user's phone detects nearby IDs and whispers, for example, 'Tom Reyes, your neighbor; knee surgery last month' from a one-line card written by the circle and managed by the caregiver. It works offline and cards expire to avoid stale information.
why_now: Cheap BLE, on-device speech and summarization, and LE Audio earbuds make this cheap to build. FDA-cleared Alzheimer's blood tests (2025) and anti-amyloid drugs are pushing diagnosis earlier, creating a fast-growing population that is cognitively capable and socially at risk for years.
revenue_model: Hardware kit, monthly subscription, and B2B circle licenses for memory cafes and senior centers. Later: plan-funded coverage.
non_obvious_insight: The privacy-safe alternative to face recognition is consent by badge: a small, fully opt-in social graph of 10-30 people that covers most of what the person meets each week. Consent is the feature, and it turns surveillance tech into hospitality.
first_30_days: Partner with three memory cafes. Make 30 badges (about $4 each) and a prototype app. Trial with five families free, measure outings per week before and after, then sell $149 kits.

title: Disposition Authority Registry for Chosen Family
one_liner: A verified registry that lets hospitals and funeral homes instantly find out who legally controls a person's body when that person is not the state's default next of kin.
customer: Solo agers, unmarried long-term partners, LGBTQ+ elders, people estranged from family, and blended-family couples pay $59 to register. Estate-planning attorneys, senior and LGBTQ+ service organizations, and hospice or palliative social work teams are the channel and secondary payers.
problem: State statutes rank who controls disposition: spouse, adult children, parents, siblings. An unmarried partner of 30 years can be shut out by a child who hasn't spoken to the deceased in a decade. When it goes wrong, the body sits in refrigeration for days or weeks while lawyers argue, and the funeral home is stuck because releasing to the wrong person means being sued. Many states allow a written designation of an agent, but witness and notary rules differ, and the signed document is in a drawer or a safe deposit box that no one can open at 2 a.m.
solution: Attorney-reviewed, state-specific designation forms completed through a remote-notary and e-sign flow. The signed document goes into a timestamped registry, with a wallet card and a phone lock-screen QR. A 24/7 verification line and API lets hospital social workers, medical examiner offices and funeral homes ask 'is there a designated agent for this person?' The designated agent is auto-notified. The record also stores preferences (cremation or burial, preferred funeral home, link to any pre-need contract).
why_now: The US has a fast-growing population of solo agers and 'elder orphans': never-married, childless, divorced or estranged. The cohort of same-sex couples who married after 2015 is now entering the age of dying. Remote online notarization and electronic signature of estate documents are now widely accepted. Healthcare advance-directive registries exist, but almost none cover disposition.
revenue_model: $59 one-time registration plus $12/year for renewal and verification upkeep. Attorney and organization white-label at $25 per registrant. Hospice, hospital and health-system site licenses at $2,000-$5,000/year for verification access. Verification is free to funeral homes so adoption is frictionless.
non_obvious_insight: The ugliest funeral disputes are almost never about money, they're about who has the pen. Funeral homes carry all the legal risk of releasing to the wrong person, so they will champion and actively check any credible registry. Everyone built registries for the living person's medical wishes, but nobody built one for the body. That is the gap where an insider watches families fight in the arrangement office.
first_30_days: Launch in three states whose statutes expressly recognize a written designation of agent. Partner with a local LGBTQ+ senior center, an elder-orphan or solo-ager meetup, and two estate attorneys who will co-host workshops. Get ten funeral homes to sign a one-page pledge to check the registry on every first call. Sell registrations at senior-center and library workshops and via a 'chosen family' landing page. Target 150-200 registrations and use the first funeral-home lookup as the case study.

title: Modern Lodges for Fraternal Insurers
one_liner: A Lodge-as-a-Service company that builds young-adult chapters for existing fraternal benefit societies, pairing initiation ritual and mutual aid with their insurance licence.
customer: Fraternal benefit societies (roughly 200 in the US, with about $328B in assets and nearly 8 million members per industry figures) that need younger members, and the millennials and Gen Z members who pay dues.
problem: State law requires fraternal benefit societies to operate through a lodge system with regular meetings and ritual, yet lodge participation and the median member's age have both drifted the wrong way. Meanwhile lonely young adults, especially men, have almost no places built on commitment, mutual aid and belonging, and few own life or disability coverage.
solution: A branded 'new lodge' layer under an existing society's licence: chapters for a specific tribe such as tradespeople, first responders or new fathers. Each has a modern initiation ritual, monthly 'work nights' of volunteer building, a small mutual-aid fund, and a term-life or disability product sold through the society. We provide recruiting, chapter software, ritual scripts and host training.
why_now: The male-loneliness conversation peaked in 2024-26, and run clubs and other third places prove appetite for group belonging. Fraternal insurers hold the capital and the licence but have lost the recruiting engine, and most have never tried a modern chapter model.
revenue_model: Per-member acquisition fee of roughly $200-500, a revenue share of first-year and renewal premium (for example 10-20%), and chapter software and licensing fees per month.
non_obvious_insight: The scarcest asset for a startup building community plus mutual aid is an insurance licence, and the scarcest asset for a fraternal insurer is young community. Fraternal law makes ritual and lodges a regulatory requirement, so what looks like cost and cringe to a founder is actually a moat. The two parties need each other and neither can buy the other's asset.
first_30_days: Email membership and innovation directors at 30 mid-sized societies. Launch one pilot lodge in a single city with 25 founding members and a paid 'charter night'. Secure a letter of intent from one society to share premium revenue.

title: Supplier-side questionnaire firewall citing the VSME cap
one_liner: A forward-to tool that answers big customers' ESG, NIS2 and EUDR questionnaires from one evidence vault and flags which questions the law says a small supplier can decline.
customer: EU SMEs and small mid-caps (under 1,000 staff) that supply larger companies, bought through accountants, tax advisors and chambers of commerce who add it as a service to their clients.
problem: Since Omnibus I took effect on 18 March 2026, CSRD-scope buyers cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than the voluntary SME standard (VSME) sets out. The VSME basic module covers business description, workforce, energy and Scope 1 and 2 emissions. The cap does not cover NIS2 security questionnaires, EUDR data, voluntary customer targets or bid competition. Suppliers still get differently formatted questionnaires from every customer and lender, and most cannot tell which asks are legally capped.
solution: Suppliers forward each customer questionnaire (Excel, PDF or portal export) to an inbox. The tool parses it and maps each question to a canonical evidence vault: VSME basic answers, energy and payroll-derived Scope 1 and 2 numbers, a NIS2-lite control evidence set, and a supplier code of conduct. It auto-drafts answers. It also classifies every question as 'inside the cap', 'outside the cap, with a cited polite decline paragraph', or 'not covered by the cap (NIS2, EUDR, voluntary)'. The vault is built by pulling data the accountant already holds. Accountants get a multi-client dashboard.
why_now: The cap is 6 months old and the VSME Delegated Act was published in July 2026, so customers' procurement teams are still sending old-format questionnaires. Germany's NIS2 law took effect on 6 Dec 2025 and BSI says regulated entities will grow from about 4,500 to about 29,500, which multiplies supplier security questionnaires. CSDDD also limits information requests to smaller firms, but application is not until 2029.
revenue_model: White-label to accountancies at EUR 15-30 per client per month, or direct at EUR 49-99 per month per SME. Add EUR 150-300 for a one-off 'initial vault build' for firms not served by an accountant.
non_obvious_insight: The crowded market sells to large buyers who send questionnaires. The legally new wedge is the supplier's right to refuse, plus the accountant, who already holds energy and payroll data and is trusted. Evidence: after 18 March 2026 large CSRD companies 'cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than ... VSME', but the same source warns that 'Nothing stops a buyer choosing the bidder who turned up with clean, current numbers' and that Scope 1 and 2 are non-negotiable, so suppliers need both a decline lever and a ready pack (https://www.dashe.ai/blog/big-customer-asked-for-your-emissions/). Suppliers to NIS2 entities 'should expect questionnaires' and sending a 300-question form is common (https://www.3rdrisk.com/blog/seven-nis2-questions-to-ask). Germany's NIS2 registration had only 38.5% compliance by the March 2026 deadline (https://www.cloudmagazin.com/en/2026/03/22/nis2-and-saas-supply-chain-compliance-gap/).
first_30_days: Collect 30 real questionnaires by offering accountants a free 'questionnaire triage' in exchange for the redacted files. Hand-map them to a 60-row canonical answer sheet. Build the classify-and-decline prototype on that set. Pitch 5 small accounting firms and 2 chamber-of-commerce sustainability desks with a live demo on a client's own questionnaire. Aim for 3 paying accountancy pilots.

title: Water Towers as Virtual Power Plants
one_liner: Aggregate municipal pump stations and elevated tanks into a controllable flexible load that dodges peak-coincident charges and earns demand-response and capacity payments, with a hard guarantee on pressure and fire reserve and an operator veto.
customer: Cities and districts that pump water, especially cities that own both the electric and water departments (common in the Midwest, Texas and the Southeast) and utilities with transmission-level or large demand-charge accounts. The buyer is the utilities director or the city manager, with the finance director as the champion.
problem: Electricity is one of the largest controllable costs for a pumped water system. Yet most pumping schedules are simple level setpoints written years ago, and operators keep tanks fat out of habit and fear. The unspoken rule is that nobody ever got fired for a full tank. Meanwhile the grid has turned pumping hours into money. Peak-coincident charges such as 4CP in ERCOT and peak load contribution tags in PJM are set by just a handful of hours per year. Capacity prices have spiked in recent auctions. Big load additions are pushing retail rates up. Water utilities are physically able to shift a large share of pumping, but no vendor is selling it to the 10-100k-population systems in a form an operator trusts.
solution: A small edge box or cloud service that reads tank levels, pump status and pressure from SCADA (OPC-UA or Modbus, read-only at first). It computes safe curtailment windows per station with hard constraints: fire and emergency reserve never touched, minimum pressure kept, projected demand over the event covered, water-age limits respected. It pre-cools tanks before predicted grid peaks and auto-releases if any constraint is threatened. Operators see one screen and can veto or end an event in one tap. Phase one is pure peak-coincident avoidance and time-of-use shifting, which needs no market enrollment. Phase two enrolls the stations as a curtailment resource through a demand-response aggregator partner or directly.
why_now: Recent PJM capacity auctions cleared at or near the price cap, on the order of $100k or more per curtailable megawatt per year before an aggregator's cut. Data center load growth is pushing capacity and transmission costs into retail rates, and RTOs and utilities are expanding demand-response programs. Edge controllers and OPC-UA gateways are cheap, and small teams can now build reliable forecasting for tank levels and peak intervals. (Auction figures are from memory. Verify current prices before pitching.)
revenue_model: 25-40% of verified savings and demand-response revenue, with no upfront cost to the utility and a small monthly platform fee. Utilities with both electric and water departments can be sold a bundled controls contract.
non_obvious_insight: The constraint is not physical but psychological and legal: operators are (rightly) terrified of a pressure or fire-flow failure. The winning product is not optimization software but a guarantee with a veto. Sell the operator the ability to stop it at any moment and the CFO the savings. Also, water and electric are often the same city, and the city has never put both budgets on one page.
first_30_days: Target three small cities that own both electric and water in ERCOT or PJM territory and have published tariffs. Get read-only SCADA access at one pump station, or historical CSV exports of tank levels and pump runs. Replay a year of the data to show what a 4CP or PLC avoidance schedule would have saved with reserves untouched. Bring that dollar figure to the city manager, and sign a shared-savings pilot on one pump station.

title: AI-Use Attestation to Keep SMB Liability Cover
one_liner: As liability policies exclude generative AI, small firms need underwriter-ready proof of AI controls to win affirmative cover, and independent agencies need a renewal ritual that keeps them relevant.
customer: Independent insurance agencies (about 37k remain) that place GL and E&O for law firms, accountants, marketing agencies, clinics and contractors, plus those SMB clients.
problem: ISO's gen-AI exclusion is already on thousands of CGL policies (Insurance Business, 2026-09-16). AI-specialist insurers target tech firms, not a dental practice using an AI receptionist. Agencies can't advise and carriers haven't said what evidence they'd accept, so clients discover the gap at claim time.
solution: A lightweight AI Use Register: discover which AI tools staff use (SSO and browser discovery), apply policy templates and human-review logging, and output a standardized attestation that a panel of MGAs and carriers agree to accept for endorsements or premium credits. Agencies white-label it into their renewal workflow.
why_now: Exclusions are spreading now, independent agencies are shrinking (39k in 2024 to 37k in 2026, Insurance Journal) yet still sell 95% of commercial insurance through humans, and insurtech's dollars (99.1% of Q2 funding is AI-centric) go to back-office tools, not SMB risk evidence.
revenue_model: $49-$149 per month per SMB, billed via the agency or the client, plus MGA per-policy referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Carriers don't yet know what evidence they want, so whoever standardizes the artifact defines it, as cyber questionnaires and scans did for Coalition and At-Bay. Agencies get a reason to call every client at renewal.
first_30_days: Interview five underwriters on what evidence they'd accept. Ship a spreadsheet-and-form v0 of the register. Sell it to 10 agencies through state agent-association chapters and get 30 SMBs onto paid plans.

title: Large-Load Water Tariff Desk for Utilities
one_liner: An advisory-plus-software desk that gives small water and wastewater utilities the tariffs, effluent valuation and contract terms to negotiate with data centers.
customer: Municipal water and wastewater utilities and councils near data-center clusters (Texas, Arizona, Ohio, Georgia, Wyoming, Nebraska), plus investor-owned utilities preparing rate cases (the 15 largest private water companies invested about $6.8B in 2025). The utility pays.
problem: Step one: states restrict potable and groundwater for data centers. Step two: developers turn to treated effluent and offer take-or-pay deals under NDA. Step three: the small utility on the other side has no large-load rate class, no reclaimed-water price, no drought-curtailment priority and no analysis of downstream users who depend on its return flows. Electric utilities built large-load tariffs 12-24 months ago, and water is next.
solution: A 'Large-Load Water Tariff Toolkit': a cost-of-service model for a new large load, minimum-take and curtailment clauses, effluent valuation (including return-flow obligations), construction cost recovery, and reporting and audit clauses matching Texas and Australian rules. Entry product: a one-page 'your effluent is worth $X per acre-foot' for every discharge-permit plant within 30 miles of a data-center cluster, built from public discharge-monitoring data.
why_now: Texas froze ERCOT approvals on Aug 3, Ohio scrapped its general permit, and the Mississippi River states are drafting a compact. Regulators are asking who funds the extra infrastructure. Developers will sign deals in months, and the utility side has no playbook.
revenue_model: $30-150k fixed-fee engagements for tariff design and effluent valuation, SaaS for the cost-of-service model, and a success fee on an executed contract.
non_obvious_insight: The party with new bargaining power is the small wastewater utility, whose effluent just became an asset, but it is the least-staffed party in the room. Advising the weaker side of a deal is where the money is when the stronger side has all the lawyers.
first_30_days: Map all discharge-permit plants near known data-center campuses using public discharge and permit data. Produce 20 one-pagers. Email utility directors and city managers, and offer a free 45-minute briefing. Aim to close two paid engagements of $30-50k.

title: Rotor Rescue: Scrapyard Magnet Pick-and-Pay
one_liner: A price-sheet-plus-gauss-meter program that pays scrapyards for magnet-dense motors and rotors they currently sell as steel and copper.
customer: Rare-earth magnet recyclers and magnet makers needing domestic recycled feed (they pay per kg with assay). Scrapyards, motor rebuilders and appliance/HVAC recyclers are the sellers.
problem: The rare-earth bottleneck is 'collection and disassembly rather than recovery chemistry.' Hard-drive magnet removal often costs more than the material is worth. Yards sell EV drive units, servo and elevator motors, and e-bike hub motors by copper and steel weight, and the NdFeB rotors go into the steel shred.
solution: Skip HDDs and target a short list of heavy, magnet-dense items. Yards get a phone app plus a $150 gauss meter that identifies magnet-bearing units and shows a payout per unit or per rotor. A mobile pull cell or the yard's own labor removes rotors. We aggregate and assay them, then sell a certified, traceable magnet-feed stream to recyclers.
why_now: The IEA puts China at about 90% of material recovery capacity. The DoD-MP deal and the Texas magnet campus create domestic pull, and DOE announced $134M for critical-mineral demonstrations in June 2026. Recyclers such as Cyclic Materials and IonicRE are funded and need feed.
revenue_model: Spread between the recycler's price per kg of assayed magnet feed and the yard payout plus pull cost. Optional premium for defense-traceable lots. Small SaaS fee for the identification and price app.
non_obvious_insight: Rare-earth economics fail on tiny magnets (HDDs) but work on a few heavy items. No one publishes a price by motor model, so yards do not know a rotor holds hundreds of grams to kilograms of NdFeB. Price discovery is the missing product, not a new chemistry.
first_30_days: Buy 5 gauss meters. Visit 10 auto shredders and motor shops and measure and photograph 200 units. Build a price sheet by model. Get an offtake LOI from one magnet recycler that needs feed. Pay 3 yards on the first 50 units and publish the results to recruit more.
